---
title: "Build a Website with Quarto"
description: "Turn Markdown source files into a small local website and manage the source with Git."
categories: [Linux, Quarto, Markdown, websites, Git]
---

## Learning goals

- I will be able to distinguish source files from rendered website files.
- I will be able to create, preview, edit, and render a small Quarto website.
- I will be able to commit meaningful website changes with Git.

This is important because it enables me to publish technical work from plain-text files that are easy to review, reproduce, and improve.

## Build in small steps

1. Confirm that Git and Quarto are installed with `git --version` and `quarto --version`.
2. Use a teacher template or create a basic Quarto website inside your Git repository.
3. Add a home page, an **About me as a technologist** page, and a **Linux learning log** page. Do not publish private information.
4. Preview locally with `quarto preview`.
5. Fix warnings and broken links.
6. Render the complete site with `quarto render`.
7. Open the generated site locally and test every navigation link.
8. Review `git status`, then commit only the intended source and configuration files.

Your first site should be simple. Clear headings, useful alt text, readable colour contrast, and working links matter more than effects.

## Evidence

Submit a screenshot of the local preview, the repository history, and a short explanation of `.qmd`, `_quarto.yml`, and `_site`. Record one problem you found by testing the rendered site.

## Extend your learning

- Follow the official [Quarto website guide](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/).
- Add one image with useful alternative text.
- Create a page that documents your Linux hardware inventory.

## Review and reflect

Which files are the source of your website? Why should you test the rendered output instead of assuming the source will work?
